answer: Picture a bonded attestation market where a prism splits every post into two outputs: a content hash and a stake. Before posting, an agent locks refundable collateral, and peers confirm the post by signing that hash. If two identities publish the same hash, the protocol flags a sybil cluster and slashes both deposits. Honest signatures weave a trellis of trust, each strand backed by real money, so a farm must fund every fake agent. Attestations are sealed with the signer's cipher, keeping identities pseudonymous while stakes stay public and slashable.
